title: Habib, the Original Dynasty: Two Rings, Zero Trades, and a Third Crown Still in Pursuit
body: Every league needs a standard, and in the Buckaroo Football League that standard has always worn Habibsters colors. Kaushal won the inaugural Buckaroo Bowl in 2023 off a 10-4 record and the No. 1 seed, scoring 1,528.8 points and setting the bar the rest of the league has been chasing ever since. Even his worst performance came that season, a 74.5-point dud against Sonny in Week 9, and he still won the title. In this league, the first chapter of history belongs to Habibi.

Then he did it again. In 2024 Habib went 11-3, grabbed the top seed for the second straight year, and claimed Buckaroo Bowl II, completing the league's only back-to-back. He also doubled his waiver activity from 16 pickups to 32, proof that the dynasty was built on hustle, not autopilot. His 4-1 career playoff record says it all: when January arrives, Kaushal plays like a UGA fan on a Saturday, and drives like he's late for one.

The 2025 season was the first time the crown slipped. The Habibsters went 8-8 and earned the No. 3 seed while piling up a career-high 1,973.6 points over the longer schedule, including his best week ever: a 151.5-point demolition of Ramon in Week 2. They finished third, a fine year for most managers and a down year for a man with two rings. Watching Sonny go from last to first and take the title only made the gap feel wider.

The managerial fingerprint is unmistakable: zero trades in four seasons. Not one. Habib builds through the draft and the wire, with 97 pickups and counting, and trusts his own guys. The head-to-heads back up the method: he's 9-2 against Mekhi, 7-2 against Alan, 8-4 against Ramon, and 6-5 against Sonny. The lone longtime thorn is Randy, who leads the series 6-5, and a rookie loss to Zoe gives him a fresh score to settle.

Now the luck has turned on him. The 2026 Habibsters sit at 3-4 with 797.8 points in the new eight-team league, and the model gives them a 15 percent shot at the title. Kaushal is still working the wire hard, with 20 pickups already, and has yet to blink on a trade. Counting out the guy who won the first two Buckaroo Bowls would be a bold move, though. Dynasties don't die quietly; they just wait for the bracket.
